hints: Focus on the shape of each molecule first, lone pairs squeeze bond angles smaller, so count bonding pairs and lone pairs.

Recall the key angles: pyramidal $\text{NH}_3$ is about $107^{\circ}$, tetrahedral $\text{CH}_4$ is $109.5^{\circ}$, trigonal planar $\text{BF}_3$ is $120^{\circ}$ and linear $\text{CO}_2$ is $180^{\circ}$.
Now arrange them from smallest to largest angle and check which series keeps rising at every step without dropping back down.
walkthrough:
**Find the shape and lone pairs**

Think like VSEPR. More lone pairs means more repulsion and a smaller bond angle.

$\text{CO}_2$ is linear with no lone pairs on carbon, $\text{BF}_3$ is trigonal planar, $\text{CH}_4$ is tetrahedral, $\text{NH}_3$ is pyramidal with 1 lone pair, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is bent with 2 lone pairs.

**Remember the standard bond angles**

These are classic values to learn by heart for the exam.

$$\text{H}_2\text{O} \approx 104.5^{\circ} < \text{NH}_3 \approx 107^{\circ} < \text{CH}_4 = 109.5^{\circ} < \text{BF}_3 = 120^{\circ} < \text{CO}_2 = 180^{\circ}$$

**Test for increasing order**

Increasing means each number must get bigger as you move right.

Only $\text{NH}_3 (107^{\circ}) \to \text{CH}_4 (109.5^{\circ}) \to \text{CO}_2 (180^{\circ})$ rises at every step, so that is the correct series.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_4$ is $109.5^{\circ}$ and $\text{BF}_3$ is $120^{\circ}$ which is an increase, but $\text{NH}_3$ is only about $107^{\circ}$ so the angle drops at the end. The trap is forgetting the lone pair on nitrogen makes ammonia smaller than methane.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is about $104.5^{\circ}$ and $\text{CO}_2$ is $180^{\circ}$ which is an increase, but $\text{BF}_3$ is only $120^{\circ}$ so the angle drops again. The trap is placing linear $\text{CO}_2$ in the middle when it is actually the largest possible angle.
options.C: Correct. $\text{NH}_3$ is pyramidal at about $107^{\circ}$ due to one lone pair, $\text{CH}_4$ is tetrahedral at $109.5^{\circ}$ with no lone pairs, and $\text{CO}_2$ is linear at $180^{\circ}$. This is a true increasing sequence: 107 < 109.5 < 180.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_3$ at about $107^{\circ}$ to $\text{CH}_4$ at $109.5^{\circ}$ is an increase, but $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at about $104.5^{\circ}$ is even smaller because it has two lone pairs. The trap is thinking water is similar to methane, when two lone pairs squeeze it the most.
